newsitem.title: UK: London a top financial centre in or out of EMU - BoE.
newsitem.headline: London a top financial centre in or out of EMU - BoE.

text.p: London will maintain its position as Europe's pre-eminent financial centre whether Britain signs up for a single currency or not, Bank of England executive director Ian Plenderleith said on Tuesday.
Plenderleith told the Capital Markets Research Institute in Tokyo there were several reasons why London could remain top dog in or out of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"There are good reasons for being confident of London maintaining its international position even if we do not join monetary union," he said.
London, he said, got business not just from Europe but North America, the Middle East, Far East and many emerging market economies.
It has gained business over the past decade even though continental European centres have modernised their financial markets.

And financial institutions have continued to set up or centralise their operations in London even though the British government's negotiated opt-out from EMU, scheduled to start in January 1999, has been well-known for years.
London will always benefit from English being the common language of business, the convenient time zone and the unbureaucratic regulatory framework.
Furthermore, London was not resting on its laurels, Plenderleith said. Advances continue to be made in improving market structure.
"The economics of international financial activity continue to point strongly in favour of concentration in one centre with London clearly the preferred choice," he said.
Even if Britain shuns the euro, Plenderleith said London's financial markets must be ready to trade it from the start.
"Across the board...preparations are in place to develop systems to trade the euro," he said and the Bank has encouraged that process.
"The result is that there is now no doubt that London will be a major centre for activity in the euro, just as it is for activity in the dollar and the yen."
